title: Finite filtered module homotopy category and filtered quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\operatorname{CFil}_f(R)$ be the full category of integer cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] equipped with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration], finite in the sense that $F^aK=K$ and $F^bK=0$ for some integers $a<b$. Morphisms are filtration-preserving chain maps. For two such maps $f,g:K\to L$, a filtered chain homotopy is a chain homotopy $h$ with $h^n(F^iK^n)\subseteq F^iL^{n-1}$ for every $i,n$, satisfying $f-g=dh+hd$. Let $\mathcal H_f(R)$ be the quotient category by filtered chain homotopy, and let $q:\operatorname{CFil}_f(R)\to\mathcal H_f(R)$ be its quotient functor. A morphism in $\mathcal H_f(R)$ belongs to $W$ if it has a filtered chain-map representative inducing a quasi-isomorphism on every associated graded complex $F^iK/F^{i+1}K$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. The restrictions and graded maps are the canonical maps of filtered objects [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction]. No bound is imposed on the cochain degrees.
